spans.s:
Phaṇa occurs in some manuscripts of the Kauṣītaki Upaniṣad,^1
and is explained as meaning an ‘ornament.’ But it is merely
a misreading of the correct word phala in the compound phala-
hastāḥ, ‘bearing fruits in their hands.’
1) i. 4. Cf. Weber, Indische Studien, 1, 398; Keith, Śāṅkhāyana Āraṇyaka,
19, n. 1.

Phāṇṭa in the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa^1 is said to denote the
first particles of butter produced by churning, ‘creamy butter.’
1) iii. 1, 3, 8. Cf. Eggeling, Sacred Books of the East, 26, 14, n. 1.
